- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast spikes; adjust forecast upward by 10–30% for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often over-anticipates recovery; reduce forecast by 15–25% for the next 5–10 days.
- Model frequently over-estimates short-term volatility after sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecasted values.
- If true outcome shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >10x from prior day), model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast for next 3 days by 20–50% if sentiment is bullish.
- Model under-forecasts mean-reversion periods when sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67); add 5–15% buffer to forecast for 5–7 days if sentiment is flat.
- For 30-day horizon, model often over-optimistically predicts high values when sentiment is bullish; cap forecast at 1.5x historical max if sentiment >0.75.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment followed by a spike, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lead time to forecast spike onset.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and history shows mean-reversion, model often over-forecasts; apply 10–20% downward correction for 3–5 days.
